issues.failure_explanation: N is defined as the total number of point evaluations used by S_Λ, i.e. the size of the support after forming the Smolyak combination. The displayed formula instead counts products of full univariate rule sizes over all Λ terms. In one dimension, ∑_{ℓ=1}^L Δ_ℓ telescopes to Q_L, so the formula gives ∑_{ℓ=1}^L n_ℓ rather than n_L. Hence the lower bound N≳M^L L^{d-1} used to obtain the logarithmic factor is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a valid support/cost estimate for the non-nested Gauss-Hermite Smolyak combination must replace the false cardinality formula, or the theorem must be weakened to a rate without the claimed logarithmic factor.
issues.overall_effect: The isotropic lower bound with the N^{-α/2}(ln N)^{...} dependence is unsupported; the isotropic part of the sparse-grid interpolation lower bound, which reuses this argument, is also unreliable.
issues.title: False Smolyak cardinality formula for total evaluations
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised logarithmic lower bound requires a new cardinality analysis not present in the source; the only source-supported fallback loses part of the claimed guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The interpolation operator is defined using zeros of H_{n_ℓ+1}, whereas the fooling function p_n is built from zeros of H_n. The proof then identifies the Gauss-Hermite quadrature Q_{n_ℓ} with the integral of the interpolant I_{n_ℓ}(p_n). These coincide only for a matching interpolatory quadrature at the same nodes, which is not the case as defined. Thus the reduction to the univariate quadrature lower bound does not prove the stated interpolation error bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reconcile the construction: either define the interpolation operator at the same zeros of H_{n_ℓ} used in the quadrature argument, or construct a fooling function vanishing at the zeros of H_{n_ℓ+1} and prove the corresponding univariate interpolation estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound for sparse-grid polynomial interpolation based on Gauss-Hermite interpolation is not established for the operator defined in the source.
issues.title: Interpolation lower bound uses mismatched nodes and quadrature
issues.why_classification: A contained change of construction or a new local univariate interpolation estimate can restore a comparable lower bound, but the current proof relies on incompatible definitions.
